verdicts.evidence: The callout (data-testid brief-insight) renders with the accent it is meant to have - background rgb(234,244,251), 3px left border rgb(61,152,211) - in both of its states. With no `## The challenge` in the file it is headed "Nobody has argued with this yet" and the body says the Studio cannot tell you whether the request names a solution because nothing here has read it. With a `## The challenge` section in the file it is headed "The assistant argued with this", shows i.icon-ai and prints that section verbatim as the argument. So the render half is real and I saw it. The generating half does not complete: pressing "Ask it to argue with this" (brief-ask-challenge) really does reach the pod - I captured the tmux pane in barn-base-extension and the full prompt is there - but claude answers "Not logged in · Please run /login" (no credential in /app/.home/.claude), so no `## The challenge` is ever written and the callout on base's own brief says nobody has argued.
verdicts.defect: Nothing in the Studio itself weighs the request against the problem statement, so the callout asks for the argument instead of asserting one. It can carry an argument the assistant writes into `## The challenge`, but the pod assistant has no credential in this environment, so on every real brief here the callout is the honest "nobody has argued yet" rather than the design's "this ticket asked for a solution, and here is why building it as written misses the point".

The accented banner (data-testid verify-framing, s-banner--success) renders above the criteria list with the lead "You are checking whether this does the job, not whether the code is any good" and the body "Reading the code is a separate step, on the review screen, and not this one. Four criterion cards render, one per card, each a full sentence about what a person can do: "The tab appears under the cluster nav without a reload", "It renders with metrics-server absent, and says why", "A 24-hour trend is readable at a glance", "Nothing on the existing cluster page moves or changes". They are parsed out of `## How we will know it worked` in BRIEF.md - the same list screen 10 edits and screen 12 summarises - and I confirmed that by reordering the criteria on screen 10 and seeing this screen walk them in the new order.

The chip (data-testid verify-progress) counts settled criteria. It read 2/4 with two answered; pressing Yes on criterion 3 took it to 3/4; pressing Can't tell on the same criterion took it back to 2/4 (a Can't tell does not settle); pressing Yes on the fourth took it to 4/4.

Each criterion has three segments with role=group. Clicking Yes on criterion 3 set aria-pressed=true on Yes and false on the other two; clicking No moved it to No only; clicking Can't tell moved it to Can't tell only - never more than one at a time. The selected colours are Yes green (badge rgb(62,140,79), card untinted), No red (badge rgb(246,71,71), card background rgb(253,236,236)), Can't tell warning amber (badge rgb(201,162,39), card untinted). The progress chip and the footer moved with every press: "3 of 4 met, 1 still to look at" -> "2 of 4 met, 1 not met, 1 still to look at" -> "2 of 4 met, 1 could not be judged, 1 still to look at". Pressing the pressed segment again clears it back to unanswered.

Set criterion 3 to Can't tell and checked all four claims. The counter did not increment (3/4 -> 2/4 when Yes became Can't tell). The footer reported it separately from a No: "2 of 4 met, 1 could not be judged, 1 still to look at." The badge stayed the plain criterion number "3" with no tick and no cross. And it does not block: with the other three answered Yes and this one Can't tell, the footer read "3 of 4 met, 1 could not be judged. Nothing is holding the sign-off open." and "Sign off on the outcome" was enabled - where a single No disables it with "1 criterion is answered No." One divergence worth recording: the badge is warning amber rgb(201,162,39), not grey. It is not red and not the Yes green, and grey rgb(242,243,245) is kept for "nobody has looked at this", which is the distinction the screen is built around.

Drove one criterion through all four states and read the badge each time: unanswered = plain number "3" on rgb(242,243,245); Yes = i.icon-checkmark on rgb(62,140,79); No = i.icon-close on rgb(246,71,71); Can't tell = plain number "3" on rgb(201,162,39). Colour and glyph both follow the verdict.

Set criterion 3 to No: the card gained verify__criterion--fail with background rgb(253,236,236), and the expanded block appeared with all three parts - the rule sentence (.verify__failed-rule), the labelled note textarea (data-testid verify-note-2) and the "Send this back to the assistant" button (verify-send-back-2). Set it back to Yes: the tint went, the rule and the send-back button disappeared. (The note field stays while it has text in it, deliberately, so a written note does not become invisible saved state.)

Answering a criterion stamps its provenance line. With the preview driven to /about, pressing Yes on criterion 3 produced `.verify__meta` = "Checked 04:55 PM · admin · /about" with an eye icon - who, when and the route the preview was on. Clearing the verdict removes the line rather than leaving a route recorded against no answer. Where a criterion failed, what happened instead is carried by the note, which is written into the brief as a blockquote under that criterion's verdict line: `- **Not met** at `/home`: Nothing on the existing cluster page moves or changes` followed by `  > w3-verify persisted note: the cluster page shifted by 4px.`

Set criterion 4 to No, typed "w3-verify persisted note: the cluster page shifted by 4px." into verify-note-3, pressed "Record the result", navigated to /barn/review and back to the verification screen: the textarea came back with the same text, read out of BRIEF.md. The hint above it says up front where it goes: "Recorded in BRIEF.md under this criterion when you record the result, so it is there for whoever opens the brief next. Sending it back puts it to the assistant as well." The author half is real - the note is in the repository file - and the assistant half is real too (see 13-verify-send-criterion-back).

The footer sentence counts and recounts. Four states observed on the same page: "2 of 4 met, 2 still to look at. The sign-off waits on the ones nobody has looked at."; with one No, "2 of 4 met, 1 not met, 1 still to look at. A No holds the sign-off open until it is answered Yes."; with that changed to Can't tell, "2 of 4 met, 1 could not be judged, 1 still to look at."; with everything Yes, "Every criterion met. Signing off records that in the brief." So the count of failing criteria drops to zero and the blocking sentence disappears.

The rule renders inline next to the failing criterion and it is precise about which of the three things it holds: "A No holds the outcome sign-off open until it is answered Yes; a \"Can't tell\" does not. The sign-off is one of the two answers the distribution gate needs, so a No holds that shut as well. It does not stop loading this into this Rancher or pushing the source to GitHub - those are deliberately ungated." I drove both halves. The sign-off half holds: with one criterion No the button was disabled with title "1 criterion is answered No..."; switching it to Can't tell enabled the button, the tint and the rule sentence went, and the footer read "Nothing is holding the sign-off open." The gate half is now real too: signing off writes signoffs.outcome into the barn-review-base ConfigMap that review.ts's distributionGate() reads, and changing a verdict deletes it again (verified against the live object).
verdicts.defect: The design's rule is about publishing and the product's main publish path is ungated by design. editor.vue's publishTo() sends `local` through publishExtension (cross-screen rule 2: "Deliberately ungated, forever") and `github` through handOverForReview, and only `distribute` goes through assertGateOpen. So a No blocks distributing a reviewed packet, not loading the extension into this Rancher. The screen says exactly that, which is honest, but it is not the promise the design makes.

verdicts.evidence: signOutcome() has a call site now and I drove it end to end. With all four criteria Yes the primary button was enabled; clicking it wrote signoffs.outcome into the barn-review-base ConfigMap FIRST - {verdict: approved, principal: local://user-btc48, name: Default Admin, at: 2026-08-23T17:01:19.636Z, sha: 243abea9..., note: the page-level note, packet: 0} - and only then the brief line "Outcome signed off by Default Admin on 2026-08-23." The masthead badge became "Signed off 2026-08-23", the footer's outcome row filled in, and the footer sentence became "Signed off on 2026-08-23 by Default Admin. Changing a verdict takes the sign-off back." With a criterion set to No the button is disabled and its title says which criteria are holding it; a forced click on the disabled button wrote nothing to the ConfigMap. The requester rule is enforced as well: with `## Who asked` naming local://someone-else and all four criteria Yes, the button stayed disabled with title "The brief records local://someone-else as the person who asked for this, and the outcome sign-off is theirs to give. You are signed in as local://user-btc48.", and a forced click left the ConfigMap's signoffs empty.

Implemented since the last pass, and read from the record rather than asserted. The footer draws two rows (data-testid verify-signoffs, verify-gate-code and verify-gate-outcome). Implemented since the last pass. The pane header (data-testid verify-preview-context) reads "The extension, running" until a criterion is pinned, then names the one it is showing - "Criterion 3" with `.verify__showing` carrying that criterion's full sentence - and it follows every "Show me" press. The live dot `.verify__dot` renders without the --off modifier while the dev server is answering, and its title reads "The dev server is answering".

The pane is a real iframe, not an image: src = /k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/barn/services/http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/, and reading into its contentDocument gave document.title "Rancher Prime - About", a live #app root and body text showing the dashboard nav with the "Base" product in it - i.e. the extension's own dev server with the build compiled in. Typing a path into the address field navigates it (/home -> /about -> /home), which a static image cannot do.

The external-link control in the preview header is an anchor rather than a button (.preview-panel__popout, title "Open this page on its own", target=_blank, href /k8s/clusters/local/api/v1/namespaces/barn/services/http:barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/about - note the href tracks the preview's current path). Clicked it: a new tab opened at exactly that URL and rendered the same page standalone, outside the panel.

Set criterion 4 to No, typed the note "w3-verify persisted note: the cluster page shifted by 4px." and clicked "Send this back to the assistant" (verify-send-back-3). Captured the pod's tmux pane before and after: afterwards it holds the prompt in full - 'Verification of the base extension found this acceptance criterion not met: "Nothing on the existing cluster page moves or changes". It was checked at /home. The reviewer\'s note: "w3-verify persisted note: the cluster page shifted by 4px.". Work out why it is not met and fix it. Do not edit BRIEF.md - the verdicts are recorded by the reviewer.' So the criterion, its route and the note all reach the assistant. Two things short of the full promise, neither a new finding: nothing on the row records that it was sent (the only feedback is a toast), and the pod's claude replies "Not logged in · Please run /login", so it cannot start work - that is the environment, not the screen.

The card is automatic - it runs off the working diff on load, with no button to press - and I drove all three of its live states by changing only the brief's non-goals. With non-goals that no added line mentions it is a green banner naming the terms it searched. With non-goals set to words that DO appear in the added lines outside BRIEF.md, it turned into an amber banner (border rgb(201,162,39)) reading "This change adds lines that mention what the brief said it was deliberately not doing. A word match is not proof of anything - it is a place to look.", with a row per hit naming the term and the files ("fixture / HARNESS.md, product.ts", "harness / HARNESS.md, product.ts"). With the section blank it says there is nothing to measure against. The heading is "Scope" with a "4 files changed" chip. Two divergences from the design worth recording: there is no "found automatically" tag anywhere on the card (the check is automatic, it just is not labelled that way), and what it flags is added lines matching the brief's own non-goals rather than "behaviour no criterion covers" - the card says so, and the code explains that the design's version would flag every file on every change.

`.verify__scope button` matched 0 elements in all three states I put the card into (clear, drifted, unstated). The card is a heading, a chip, a banner and a term list. `grep -rn "Add it to the brief" pkg/barn` returns 0.
verdicts.defect: The drift warning has no actions. There is no way to amend the brief from here, so an accepted drift stays flagged.

verdicts.evidence: Same enumeration, including while the card was in its drifted state with two hits showing: no buttons anywhere in `.verify__scope`. The only outbound action on the screen is the per-criterion "Send this back to the assistant", which lives in the failed-criterion block.
verdicts.defect: No reject action on the scope card. Nothing on screen 13 can request a change that strips a behaviour.

verdicts.evidence: Enumerated every button under `.verify`: Back to the queue, Open the brief, Yes/No/Can't tell x4, Show me x4, Back to the workspace, the preview's Back/Forward/Reload and its width chip, Ask the assistant to check, Record the result, Sign off on the outcome. No capture control. `grep -rn "Capture this as evidence" pkg/barn` returns 0.
verdicts.defect: No way to snapshot the preview. The provenance line exists but is written by pressing a verdict - it records the clock and the preview's route at that moment, which is not an artefact anybody can look at later.

verdicts.evidence: `document.querySelectorAll(".verify input[type=file]")` returned 0 on the loaded screen, and `grep -rn 'type="file"' pkg/barn --include=*.vue` finds exactly one, in components/studio/AssistantPanel.vue, a different screen. `grep -rn "Attach a screenshot" pkg/barn` returns 0.
verdicts.defect: No upload control and no attachment model. A verdict can carry a typed note, a route and a timestamp; it cannot carry a file.

verdicts.evidence: A text scan of the whole `.verify` element for "take your word for it" returned false, and `grep -rn "take your word" pkg/barn` returns 0. There is no capture button for such a sentence to sit above. What the screen does say is different: the framing banner explains the job, and the note hint says the note is "Recorded in BRIEF.md under this criterion when you record the result".
verdicts.defect: The sentence is not in the product. Nothing explains that captured evidence travels with the verdict, because nothing is captured.

verdicts.evidence: `.verify select, .verify [role=combobox], .verify .vs__dropdown-toggle` matched 0 elements. The preview panel's only controls are Back, Forward, Reload, a path field, a width chip and the pop-out link. The preview is the extension's own dev server inside its pod (proxied at /k8s/clusters/local/.../barn-base-extension:8005/proxy/), which has no notion of a target cluster, and `grep -rn "imported-eu" pkg/barn` returns 0.
verdicts.defect: No cluster chooser and no annotation about the current cluster. The preview is bound to one dev server; pointing it at another cluster is not something the product can do.

verdicts.evidence: A text scan of `.verify` for "Send the whole list" returned false and `grep -rn "Send the whole list" pkg/barn` returns 0; the button enumeration above has no such control. The two footer actions are "Ask the assistant to check" (which puts the outstanding criteria to the pod's claude and explicitly does not move the change) and "Record the result".
verdicts.defect: No single action returns the whole list to the author, and there is no per-change queue state for it to move into.

verdicts.evidence: One of the three. Enumerated `header button` on /barn/extensions/base/verification: "Local Cluster icon local", "Open notification center", "Open user menu". The bell opens the notification centre (a populated .notification-dropdown). `header [class*=apps], header .icon-apps` matched 0 elements and there is no three-dot control in the header - screen 13 has no .icon-actions on the page at all.
